summary: Four sequenced cuts across the Phase 5e arc this session, all pushed to claude/next-steps-xzmdk. 5e-iv shipped the read-only Lattice screen at /lattice surfacing recovery cohort + handshakes + memberships in one view with a Cohort cross-reference badge. 5e-iii-b-2 flipped the wallet to write v2 recoverable backups by default while keeping v1 backward compatibility on unlock — every save from this branch onward mints a v2 RecoverableEncryptedBlob, every legacy v1 blob on disk still unlocks via the existing path. 5e-iii-c-α added the library seam for K_data preservation across saves (unwrapKData + encryptRecoverableWithKData + Wallet.exportRecoverableWithKData) so cohort-distributed Shamir shares stay valid as the operator keeps using the wallet. 5e-iii-c-β wired it through the wallet save loop: unlock extracts K_data, WalletProvider holds it in a ref alongside the passphrase, every save threads it back through saveWallet, and the idle-lock + sign-out paths clear it with the passphrase. The keys-never-leave audit gained kData in its SECRET_NAMES list as defense-in-depth.

why.text: Operator's directive: 'fire up and take over on next steps knock out what you can as long as you see the line' followed by 'continue on and pick off the road map pieces.' The locked sequence from the Phase 5e brief made each next step obvious. 5e-iv was the rendering-shaped cut on top of the cohort declaration. 5e-iii-b-2 was the wallet-side wiring of the library half of v2 that the prior session shipped. The K_data-preservation problem surfaced during re-grounding for 5e-iii-c — without it, every save invalidates the cohort's shares, so the design must hold K_data across saves or the cascade is decorative. Library cut α first (atomic, testable), wallet wiring β second (the seam in action).

5e-iii-b-2 (52e317f): Wallet.exportRecoverable + restoreFromRecoverable + restoreFromKData; WalletBlob union threaded through localStore + walletStore + remoteStore; createWallet + saveWallet + downloadEncryptedBackup mint v2; unlockWallet dispatches on blob.v; tapit-attest +4 tests.

5e-iii-c-α (367e909): encryption.ts gains unwrapKData + encryptRecoverableWithKData; Wallet gains exportRecoverableWithKData. tapit-attest +9 tests (round-trip, length enforcement, salt/IV refresh, save-loop preservation).

5e-iii-c-β (6b52e3c): unlockWallet + createWallet + saveWallet return {wallet, kData}; WalletProvider threads kData through 4 save call sites; idle-lock + sign-out clear it; keys-never-leave audit catches kData stray logs.
outcome.tests_passing: wallet 36/36 across all cuts; tapit-attest 137/141 after 5e-iii-b-2 (4 new wallet v2 tests pass; 4 skipped network-deps), 146/150 after 5e-iii-c-α (9 more tests pass).
outcome.notes: [P-001] 5e-iv shipped Lattice at /lattice — three sections (cohort/people/orgs), cross-section Cohort badge on ConnectionCards. [P-002] 5e-iii-b-2 shipped v2-as-default with v1 backward compat — first save after a v1 unlock automatically migrates the on-disk blob. [P-003] 5e-iii-c-α shipped the K_data preservation library primitives + Wallet wrapper + 9 tests. [P-004] 5e-iii-c-β wired K_data through the save loop; 4 call sites updated, idle-lock + sign-out clear it, audit catches stray logs. [P-005] All four gates green on all four cuts; tapit-attest vendor 29.14 KB gz (under 35 KB), WalletProvider 6.33 KB gz (under 7 KB), LatticeScreen 2.12 KB gz (under 5 KB). [FEEDBACK→Foreman]: the K_data architecture (preservation across saves; rotation only on explicit cohort re-publish) is the design crux that fell out of re-grounding — worth flagging in the next brief refresh because it constrains how cohort rotation will work. Recommend the next session opens with a sub-brief for 5e-iii-c-γ: recovery-share envelope shape, cohort-publish distribution flow, peer-side inbox auto-routing.

uncertainty: Did not exercise any of these cuts in a browser. The v1→v2 migration is the highest-risk path — the operator's deployed wallet has a v1 blob and the next save under this branch will rewrite it as v2. Reverting to a pre-5e-iii-b-2 branch after that point requires manual blob rollback. Recommend the operator test on a fresh Supabase identity first OR back up their cloud blob row before deploying. The K_data preservation design has the operator's deployed wallet picking up kData=null on first unlock (because their on-disk blob is v1), minting fresh K_data on first save, then preserving it — the migration is automatic but irreversible; a v1 blob backup is the only way home if something goes wrong.
